# Moneo: Deep Weed Audit — Tests, PR History, Documentation, Tooling

**Audit date:** 2026-11-09  
**Repository:** https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo  
**Audited branch/HEAD:** `main` at `ce7995b817ec45c719527d7d3dcfcbe7400f214e`  
**Status:** Findings and implementation specification; **no changes made** to the repository.  
**Audience:** Codex / Claude Code / maintainers.  
**Objective:** Reduce maintenance friction and false confidence while increasing protection against genuinely expensive financial, privacy, data-loss, and authorization failures.

> **Read this first:** This is a repository/PR **static audit**, not a claim that the suite was executed on the user's computer. I read GitHub PR metadata for **131 PRs (128 merged; 3 closed unmerged)**, examined important PR bodies and file changes, inventoried the current tree, and inspected representative high-risk tests, runner configuration, instructions and production code. I did **not** execute Docker, Vitest, Playwright, live provider tests, or measure performance. Recommendations labeled *suspected* require a local red/green reproduction before editing behavior. Do not delete tests merely because they are old, large, or mocked.

---

## 0. Executive decision

**Do not delete the entire test suite.** The principal weeds are **selection/orchestration, QA isolation, shared mutable state, implementation-coupled tests, misleading test names, and missing failure-oriented tests**. The best approach is to replace a small number of weak checks, remove their old forms *after* replacement coverage passes, and organize the remaining tests by purpose.

**Five first moves, in order:**

1. **Make test execution safe:** require explicit dedicated QA identity, isolate any browser tests with mutations, refuse to run a browser suite against the owner's workspace or an unverified existing server.
2. **Repair acceptance selection:** optional real-AI/MCP tests must not cause a mandatory zero-skip suite to fail; remove dynamic test skips caused by mutable initial UI state.
3. **Replace implementation-text testing:** retire source-string assertions in `scripts/acceptance.test.ts` once behavioral runner tests exist.
4. **Tie regression coverage to actual severe PR incidents:** deployed `PT409` conflict behavior, cross-screen net-worth parity, artifact exfiltration boundaries, OAuth host-ID contract, import undo/re-import idempotency, and self-host recovery.
5. **Split fast vs DB vs browser vs release vs provider vs performance:** preserve strong SQL/finance/RLS/security tests; avoid one oversized gate for all changes.

**Avoid:** building a second giant testing framework; deleting all unit tests; deleting SQL regression fixtures; reintroducing real AI calls in default CI; changing production data to satisfy test fixtures; editing previously applied migrations; running `docker compose down -v`.

---

## 1. Inventory of what exists now

| Type | Current repository inventory | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| Vitest `*.test.ts(x)` files | **295** | Mixed unit, components, API-route, contract, some live-database tests |
| Playwright `*.spec.ts` files | **60** | **52** `.gated`, **7** `.mocked`, **1** `.smoke` |
| `supabase/tests/*.sql` | **53** test SQL files + **2** fixture SQL files | Migration/RLS/SQL regression tests; not all individual test cases counted |
| `.live.test.ts` | **8** of the 295 Vitest files | Opt-in tests guarded by environment flags |
| Performance tools | **3** (`bench-cards.mts`, `perf-pages.mjs`, `perf-interactions.mjs`) | Measurement scripts, **not** enforced budgets |
| Additional integration tools | Workflow runtime tests, migration replay, SQL concurrency runners | Valuable but some run only through nondefault commands |
| GitHub Actions under `.github/workflows` | **0 files** in audited tree | No checked-in Actions CI policy |
| Static QA/agent setup | `AGENTS.md`, `e2e/README.md`, `supabase/tests/README.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.entire/settings.json` | Some policies describe more assurance than the runner actually provides |

**Existing commands:** `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run acceptance:fast`, `npm run acceptance:required`, `npm run check:privacy`. `pretest` and `prelint` invoke the privacy filename check. `playwright.config.ts` runs Chromium Desktop Chrome and can reuse an existing dev server on port 3000. No dedicated `typecheck` npm script or CI pipeline is defined in `package.json`.

**Preserve as high-value coverage:** financial amount/currency/rounding tests, immutable source and undo tests, `lib/finance/net-worth-source.test.ts`, balance and reservation live tests, SQL replay + RLS (`workspace-isolation.sql`), concurrency tests, authorization-scope revocation in `app/api/chat/route.test.ts`, and hostile artifact-browser tests. These guard costly bugs and are not merely decoration.

---

## 2. PR archaeology: real evidence of weeds

| PR and evidence | Pattern exposed | What test should now exist |
|---|---|---|
| [#91 — Fix stale browser tests and QA login](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/91): reported **30 browser failures and 27 skipped**, already stale before code cleanup | Browser assertions and auth fixtures drift with UI; “more E2E” can turn into test maintenance | Stable role-based journey tests and deterministic identity/setup; disallow arbitrary skip-as-success |
| [#140 — User-testing audit repairs](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/140): **no single fully green `acceptance:required` run**; one reported full suite was **82/83**, different tests failed in slow patches | The all-or-nothing release gate is noisy and hard to interpret; state/timing coupling | Fresh QA workspace per suite; independent deterministic E2E; duration/flake telemetry; real readiness signals |
| [#146 — Self-hosted migration](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/146): 157 files affected; removed login/auth routes and tests; reported **18 test cleanup failures** and remaining browser failures | Huge platform migration invalidated old suite assumptions; install/update/recovery is not covered by the normal browser suite | Disposable first-install + upgrade + restart + restore smoke with preserved secrets/financial history |
| [#131 — SQLSTATE `40001` retry storm](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/131): stale conflict allegedly retried ~**1,100 times/s for 18 hours**, exhausting connections | Code can pass source checks while real HTTP/database semantics are catastrophically wrong | Real PostgREST conflict returns exactly one HTTP 409 promptly, without retry storm or connection starvation |
| [#132 — Cross-surface money totals](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/132): Overview, Accounts and Wealth gave contradictory totals | Per-component tests can all pass while the product violates a shared financial invariant | One seed drives Overview/Accounts/Wealth/chat/tool values; all match the same deterministic balance basis |
| [#160 — Artifact Page protection](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/160); [#142 closed unmerged](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/142): generated Pages could navigate/exfiltrate financial data | Passing generated HTML/syntax checks is not a security or correctness guarantee | Real frame-route headers + hostile HTML in Chromium; forbidden network/navigation; no secrets or financial data outbound |
| [#174 — ChatGPT sign-in rejection](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/174): bare UUID instead of `urn:uuid:` host identifier | Mocked OAuth calls overlooked external-provider contract | Deterministic host ID contract, migrated-ID test, and isolated opt-in real-provider smoke (never in default CI) |
| [#124 — Voice performance regression](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/124): +94 KB JS, hidden tab polling, 68 RSC requests/12s, CLS regression | Green functional tests do not detect performance/cost regressions | Browser request-count/polling and CLS budgets with synthetic QA data and repeatable baseline |
| [#57 — E2E fixture mismatch](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/57): mocked conversation history inconsistent with reply; import assertions raced inspection | Mocks can fabricate impossible states and make tests fail for the wrong reason | Shared API schema/factory contracts; await operation completion, no arbitrary timers |
| [#26 — Fast versus required acceptance](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/26) and [#43 — live DB gate](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/43) | Good intent (skip detection/provenance) implemented with overly broad selection and source-string coupling | Explicit suite manifests + report/exit-code behavior tests, not grepping runner source |
| [#138 — Artifacts re-architecture](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/138): old builder routes and tests removed; new chat + QuickJS cards | Old implementation-era tests and docs must be audited after each major architectural pivot | Regression tests for today’s artifact workflow, not old builder implementation |
| [#19 — Removed private bank inputs](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/19) | Filename gate alone does not prevent embedded secrets in code/docs | Credential and sensitive-content scanning on staged/tracked files |

**Interpretation:** Frequent PRs that repair test fixtures are not automatically bad, but #91, #140, and #146 together support a systemic issue with E2E maintenance. #131, #132, #160 and #174 show genuine missing cross-boundary assertions. Prioritize those missing assertions over cosmetic test-count targets.

---

## 3. Findings — confirmed code facts, risk and fix

### P0-01 — Mandatory acceptance includes intentionally optional tests

**Evidence:** `scripts/acceptance.mjs` collects every root `e2e/*.spec.ts` except `core-journey.gated.spec.ts`, then `assertRequiredResults('playwright')` rejects **any** skipped test. Yet `e2e/net-worth-chat.gated.spec.ts` skips without `E2E_REAL_AI`; `e2e/scalable-trading.gated.spec.ts` skips without a local `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN`; `e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` skips at runtime if Goals is already first. The runner clears `OPENAI_API_KEY` and does not set the two opt-in variables.

**Impact:** a working application can fail required acceptance for a test it never intended to execute. Also risks live-provider calls when accidental credentials leak into the environment.

**Change:** Explicit allowlists for `qa:smoke`, `qa:db`, `qa:browser-required`, `qa:provider`, `qa:performance`; reject **unexpected** skips only within the relevant required list. Never select opt-in tests for regular browser acceptance. Test that the manifest includes *every* intended required test and excludes every opt-in test. Do not silently exclude new specs: new specs must be classified intentionally.

**Proof:** run `playwright --list` for each manifest; required suite in correct test environment executes with zero skips; optional tests appear only on explicit invocation; no real-provider request during default tests.

### P0-02 — Browser QA identity is not fail-closed

**Evidence:** `e2e/agent-team.mocked.spec.ts`, `e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts`, `e2e/import-control.mocked.spec.ts` use the QA cookie **if** present and otherwise proceed. Self-hosted `proxy.ts` automatically signs in the owner. `e2e/service-keys.mocked.spec.ts` *does* explicitly skip without QA session, showing contradictory policy. `e2e/README.md` says mocked specs need no session and tests never touch the owner workspace.

**Impact:** **risk**, not proven incident: browser tests lacking QA cookies may execute as the automatically signed-in owner. Mocking an API route does not necessarily isolate every server-side read and action.

**Change:** Central `e2e/qa-fixture.ts` with **mandatory** verified QA cookie/owner ID, dedicated synthetic workspace and guarded base URL. No test should run without explicit QA marker. For credential-free tests, serve an **isolated synthetic test server**, never the personal Moneo app. Block writes and fail if the workspace is not marked QA. Add negative tests confirming absent/wrong session refuses before opening browser.

**Proof:** tests cannot start with no QA cookie, expired cookie, different owner or wrong base URL; only synthetic workspace rows change; cleanup checks after each suite.

### P0-03 — E2E test runner may reuse an unintended development server

**Evidence:** `playwright.config.ts`: `reuseExistingServer: !production && !process.env.CI` on port 3000; `E2E_BASE_URL` can point elsewhere. Combined with owner auto-sign-in, this is a potentially unsafe default.

**Change:** Dedicated QA port and explicit readiness/identity response (not just port-open). Disallow shared-dev-server reuse for DB-mutating E2E unless verified as QA. Require `MONEO_TEST_INSTANCE=1` / QA owner marker checked server-side. Make production-build tests start their own known server.

**Proof:** a non-QA server running on the port makes tests abort **before requests**.

### P0-04 — QA reset bypasses database triggers/foreign keys

**Evidence:** `scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset` checks `qa_test='e2e-auth'`, then uses `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica` and dynamically deletes by `workspace_id`, `actor_id`, `user_id`, `created_by` across all public tables.

**Impact:** Deliberately disabling triggers/FKs can hide real integrity violations, and generic per-column sweeping is difficult to reason about after schema changes. Not evidence that the owner has been harmed; the QA-user guard is good.

**Change:** Prefer disposable DB/isolated Docker or authenticated `reset_workspace()` with exact workspace/owner verification, full cleanup receipts and FK checks enabled. Keep explicit rejection for non-QA users. Fail on unexpected tables, never silently broaden deletion.

**Proof:** seed one QA user and an unrelated user; reset QA; other user data bit-for-bit unchanged; FK/invariant checks remain active; repeatable cleanup even after failed test.

### P1-05 — Acceptance tests assert runner source text

**Evidence:** `scripts/acceptance.test.ts` scans test source and asserts that `scripts/acceptance.mjs` contains exact strings like `RUN_*_DB_TESTS: "1"` and `run("units", ... "--no-file-parallelism")`.

**Impact:** A safe formatting/refactor can fail; a script containing the expected text in an unused branch could pass. Source checks are not proof of execution.

**Change:** Export a pure suite manifest from the runner and test it as data; run a fake runner with success/fail/skip/flaky fixtures in isolated temp dirs, assert exit code, selected files, reports, absence of unexpected skips and provenance behavior. Keep the direct `assertProductionBuild` / `assertRequiredResults` unit cases (valuable).

**Proof:** harmless refactor doesn't fail; removing DB flag from effective runtime config *does* fail.

### P1-06 — Shared mutable E2E session and state

**Evidence:** `e2e/auth-refresh.gated.spec.ts` writes refreshed cookies into the shared `e2e/.auth.json`; browser suites use a persistent QA workspace and require manual `scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset`; `e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` dynamically skips if Goals already first. PR #140 recorded run-to-run variable failures.

**Change:** Every stateful test should construct its starting data, use unique entities/workspace (or snapshot/reset per group), and not rewrite shared storage state. Convert Goals-first skip to deterministic arrangement or test both move/no-move paths. Collect per-test duration and retry/flake metadata.

**Proof:** randomize suite order; run twice; run parallelizable mocked tests in parallel; no ordering dependency or skip.

### P1-07 — Monolithic and mixed-fidelity browser journey

**Evidence:** `e2e/core-journey.gated.spec.ts` mixes real database import, a real AI chat request, mocked inspect mapping and mocked deep-analysis completion, with 240-second test timeout. It is entirely excluded from required acceptance, although its non-AI part provides valuable product coverage. `e2e/scalable-trading.gated.spec.ts` combines a local MCP stand-in with a real model call.

**Change:** Extract **deterministic app workflows** (import → ledger → re-import, card approval → recorded mutation, chat-tool invocation with stub model), and keep separate **opt-in provider evaluations**. Mark every mock boundary explicitly in test names/report. Never claim a model integration was verified because an API response was mocked.

**Proof:** deterministic journeys pass offline on synthetic QA data; provider checks are separately reported with identity, model and cost labels.

### P1-08 — Behavioral regression absent for catastrophic SQL retry semantics

**Evidence:** `supabase/tests/conflict-errcode.test.ts` is a small regex scanning only migration files lexically later than `202610310001` for one exact `errcode = '40001'` pattern. #131 was a runtime PostgREST retry failure.

**Change:** **Keep** this cheap guard, but add a deployed-PostgREST contract test causing a stale version conflict: assert one timely 409, returned error shape, bounded query count, no sustained retries, and a concurrent independent request still succeeds. Also test equivalent variations of SQLSTATE-raising syntax and all public conflict functions.

**Proof:** the old dangerous behavior fails the new test; correct `PT409` passes. No real owner data.

### P1-09 — Mocked security checks aren't a complete HTTP-boundary guarantee

**Evidence:** `e2e/artifact-page-protection.mocked.spec.ts` is a useful browser test with hostile HTML, attempted `fetch`, beacon, image, popup, iframe/form and navigation. `lib/ai/artifact-data.test.ts` tests CSP strings. However the mocked harness doesn't guarantee the deployed `/ai/artifacts/[id]/frame` route sends exactly the intended CSP/cache headers, auth checks and data-scope checks.

**Change:** Keep both tests. Add a separate **real route HTTP response** test with QA session: inspect actual `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, sandbox/no-same-origin, unauthorized/foreign artifact denial, and re-run hostile payload in actual `ArtifactFrame` with network requests captured.

**Proof:** malicious page cannot send data, navigate to a foreign origin, load remote scripts or access parent cookies; legitimate local charts still render.

### P1-10 — Financial semantic correctness lacks a single cross-system fixture

**Evidence:** #132 repaired mismatched totals; `lib/finance/net-worth-source.test.ts` now tests cross-reader parity with a mocked query interface. Very good, but a real DB/RLS/route/browser multi-surface test is a different boundary. Cards also validate rendering/syntax rather than arbitrary AI-written finance arithmetic.

**Change:** Reuse **one deterministic financial oracle**/fixture for accounts, balances, transfers, pending holds, FX, investments, debt and stale values. Verify API + Home + Accounts + Wealth + chat tool + artifact data outputs. Use property/metamorphic tests: adding balanced internal transfers doesn't change total net worth; same-currency rounding exact; re-import same source doesn't duplicate. For AI-generated cards, define which finance sums **must** come from precomputed trusted data, not model-authored arithmetic.

**Proof:** intentional double-counting/missing-account mutants are killed. Avoid asserting implementation internals or formatting that is not contractual.

### P1-11 — Security/privacy gate's name overstates coverage

**Evidence:** `scripts/check-private-data.mjs` reads `git ls-files -z`, rejects extensions and ignored private directories, but **does not read file contents**. `AGENTS.md` says no secrets/private statements in repo; `pretest`/`prelint` running this script can convey false assurance. #19 removed tracked private bank files.

**Change:** Keep filename guard (valuable). Add secret scanning/content signatures for credential patterns and accidental embedded financial identifiers; support explicit documented allowlist for synthetic fixtures. Run on staged content and all commits/PR diff where feasible, with redacted output. Don't upload private data to a third-party scanner without explicit approval.

**Proof:** synthetic fake token/IBAN embedded in `.ts` or `.md` is flagged, harmless fixture passes, scanner never prints the secret.

### P1-12 — First-install / update / recovery regression untested

**Evidence:** #146 moved deployment to local Docker, data volumes and `.env` secrets; `scripts/setup.mjs` applies migrations and keeps existing secrets; test inventory has migration replay and UI tests but no complete disposable install → update → restore test.

**Change:** In a disposable Docker project and throwaway temp directory, assert fresh install, restart, idempotent setup, migration upgrade, backup/restore and preservation of encrypted tokens/financial rows (using test-only keys). Never run destructive setup/restore against personal volumes. Add backup implementation as a separate project task if not present.

**Proof:** restore exact synthetic ledger + secrets, reinstall doesn't overwrite keys, wrong key fails clearly, volume reset is never used on owner data.

### P2-13 — Fixed sleeps and overly broad timeout budgets

**Evidence:** `e2e/artifact-page-protection.mocked.spec.ts` waits 1,500 ms (for a known delayed attack); `e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts` simulates a 20-second response delay; multiple gated specs allow 180–600 seconds. Timing itself isn't a failure but often makes feedback slow and nonrepeatable.

**Change:** Use deferred promises, clock control or `expect.poll` at the *specific* observable event. Keep time-based waits only when the time threshold is itself under test. Use sane per-class timeouts and capture traces on failure.

### P2-14 — Narrow UI tests are sometimes presented as broader integration proof

**Evidence:** `e2e/agent-team.mocked.spec.ts` checks an import-history link to `/ai/agents?import=...`, not whether an agent runs. `e2e/core-journey.smoke.spec.ts` asserts `/api/health` booleans/env shape and a navigation, not actual DB/AI service health. Its OpenAI network listener observes browser requests, not necessarily server-side provider calls.

**Change:** Accurately rename or move link checks into component tests; keep a clear browser smoke verifying real route access. Rename `health configuration` vs `health dependency readiness`; don't label either as real provider validation.

### P2-15 — Performance measurements can mutate QA settings and are not gates

**Evidence:** `scripts/perf-interactions.mjs` executes `update public.workspace_settings set ai_models = ai_models - 'chat'` for the QA workspace and does not restore that value in the script. `perf-pages.mjs` and `bench-cards.mts` report medians/p95 but do not enforce budgets. PR #124 found regressions ordinary unit tests missed.

**Change:** Use disposable QA snapshot; restore state in `finally`; isolate benchmark process from normal test DB. Establish a few reliable budgets: hidden-tab request count, artifact script bundle, Home CLS and number of duplicate network requests. Compare to committed reference baselines **with tolerances** instead of brittle fixed milliseconds from one machine.

### P2-16 — Documentation and AI-agent instructions have drift

**Evidence:** `e2e/README.md` says `.mocked` specs need no saved session, while `e2e/service-keys.mocked.spec.ts` requires QA auth; `e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts` refers to `prompt.md §46` which is absent from tracked `main`; `AGENTS.md` says E2E never touches owner workspace without establishing fail-closed verification. `.claude/settings.json` still attaches numerous `entire` lifecycle hooks and `.entire/settings.json` enables Entire telemetry/checkpoints; this is distinct from the **test** acceptance gate. `docs/artifacts-video-script.md` says real balances may be displayed in a recording.

**Change:** Update docs only to current behavior and test matrix; remove dead `prompt.md` citations; require synthetic demo data for public recordings by default. Audit whether Entire hooks actually provide useful checkpoints—if not, simplify/disable hooks **separately** from the acceptance test rewrite, preserving user-preferred session capture. Keep Next.js generated agent rules if Next itself rewrites them; avoid endless diff churn.

### P2-17 — Missing explicit CI and test categorization

**Evidence:** no `.github/workflows` files, only local scripts. `playwright.config.ts` has a single Chromium desktop project. Tests exist for mobile behavior but the default project is not a distinct mobile browser profile.

content.text:
I agree with the audit's safety findings. I disagree with its main remedy: it would add about 16 new test suites, six `qa:*` commands, suite manifests and mutation testing. That's a second test framework, which is the opposite of what Theo describes. It also mostly skips the layer agents actually copy from, which is the unit tests.

## What I checked myself

- **`npm test` on current main:** 1,591 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped (the 8 `.live` DB files), 69 s wall-clock. One file, `lib/ai/voice-call-controller.test.ts`, takes 24 s of that.
- **Size:** 296 Vitest files and 60 Playwright specs, about 22k lines of tests against about 36k lines of source. There is no CI at all (`.github/` doesn't exist), so nothing stops a PR that breaks tests.
- **Where the sprawl came from:** the original `prompt.md` §46 and `orchestrator-prompt.md` (Oct 1). They said *"every in-scope clause maps to acceptance evidence"*, *"a skipped test is not a pass"* and *"mark items complete only with evidence"*. Agents read that as "write a test per requirement sentence". That's why there are names like `mne024.gated.spec.ts` and 52 gated E2E specs, and why `acceptance:required` rejects any skip. Those prompts are deleted, but the tests they produced keep getting copied.
- **From your past sessions:**
  - On 2026-10-26 you asked to "remove those 14 tests so it doesn't always fail". Four commits deleted them instead of mocking the model. That fixed the symptom, not the cause.
  - On 2026-11-05: "if only this failed and it's a test, just run this." Agents learn that the gates can be bypassed.
  - PRs #91 and #140 were mostly about repairing E2E, and #140 never got a fully green run.

## Weeds the audit missed (Vitest)

1. **Page tests that check copy text with heavy mocking.** 42 of the 46 `.test.tsx` files render static HTML and assert strings. For example, `app/page.test.tsx` mocks 13 modules and then checks `toContain("Aggregate headroom")`. Changing a label breaks them, while a broken data flow wouldn't, because the data is mocked. Agents copy this pattern for every new page.
2. **Tests that grep migration files for text:**
   - `app/plan/assumptions.test.ts` (third block)
   - `lib/finance/chat-publication-migration.test.ts`
   - `supabase/tests/conflict-errcode.test.ts`
   - the two source-text tests in `scripts/acceptance.test.ts`

   These check that SQL *contains* a string, not that it behaves correctly. `currency-precision-contract.test.ts` also reads a migration, but it's a real alignment check, so keep it.
3. **Slow tests that wait on time.** `voice-call-controller.test.ts` waits on timers (`wait(10_000)` and similar). It should be about 1 s.

## What to remove

| Remove | Why |
|---|---|
| Migration and source grep tests (list above) | They prove text exists, not behaviour |
| `acceptance:required` and its zero-skip gate (`scripts/acceptance*.mjs`) | A leftover of the orchestrator prompt; it fails for tests it never meant to run |
| Copy-text page tests where nothing money-related is asserted | Keep the ones that assert amounts or which account is shown; drop label-only assertions |
| Most of the 52 gated E2E specs | Keep about 8–10 real journeys (import → undo → re-import, card approval, net worth parity, two-user isolation, artifact protection, theme contrast, bad links). The rest are "one spec per audit finding" and rot |
| `agent-team.mocked.spec.ts`, the health-config part of `core-journey.smoke` | A full browser run to check one link |

**Keep** the `lib/finance` and import tests, the SQL/RLS tests, migration replay, the concurrency tests, the `.live` DB tests, the chat route scope tests and `artifact-page-protection`. They guard real money and privacy failures.

I'd do the deletion as one PR with the list in the description. Each deleted file gets either "covered by X" or "asserts copy only".

## What to add (short list)

1. **CI on every PR** (one workflow): privacy check, lint, `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest`, build. It needs no `.env`, DB or network. This is the fence for "no PR with failing tests".

## Goal
The owner wants this codebase to be an excellent place for AI coding agents to work: they should move fast, not get blocked by noisy, slow or flaky checks, and not copy bad patterns that make the codebase sloppier over time. Do your own independent look. Nobody has told you what is wrong; form your own view from the code, tests, docs, scripts and git history.

## Background: lessons from a talk by Theo (T3) on being a codebase "gardener"
- Code quality is an organisational setup problem. When someone produces bad code because docs or existing examples were misleading, fix the docs and examples (the cause), not only the one PR (the symptom). Make the right path the easy path.
- Old slop blocks new work: messy legacy code and patterns slow every later contributor, human or AI.
- Friction hurts agents more than humans: slow dev-server startup, slow or heavy test runs and slow pipelines waste agent time and tokens and discourage merging.
- Slop multiplies fast: agents copy what they see. Bloated, pointless tests make agents write more pointless tests. Theo deleted about half of T3 Code's unit tests (about 11,000 tests) in one PR; only 4 had to come back and no regressions were missed.
- When a pointless test slips into a PR, ask the agent why it wrote it, then fix the repo guidance that triggered it.
- Add targeted "wooden stakes": a few fast, automated checks on what really matters (e.g. a CI check that flags payload/performance regressions with a clear red X), rather than many weak checks.
- With fewer blockers, PR throughput went from a handful per day to hundreds.

## Project facts
Moneo is a self-hosted personal-finance app (Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Postgres plus Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Storage in Docker, Drizzle, Workflow, Vitest, Playwright, Vercel AI SDK). Read `AGENTS.md` first; its safety rules apply to you. In particular:
- Never run anything against the owner's real workspace or data. Do not run `npm run setup`, Docker commands, Playwright/E2E, `.live` DB tests, perf scripts or anything that touches a database or real AI/bank/Scalable services.
- You MAY run hermetic checks: `npx vitest run` (or a subset; there is no `.env` in this worktree, so DB-backed `.live` tests skip), `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`. `node_modules` is installed.
- You may read git history (`git log`, `git show`, including deleted files) to find where patterns came from.

1. **Repair required acceptance before treating it as a merge gate.** It includes an optional, real-model Scalable spec whose missing prerequisites cause skips—and required acceptance rejects skips.
2. **Require hermetic checks on PRs.** This checkout has no `.github` workflows. Local acceptance reports cannot themselves prevent merging.

4. **Add one deterministic performance budget.** The existing import throughput script records latency but does not fail on latency regression.
5. **Improve test guidance before broadly deleting tests.** The suite takes about 29 seconds; its financial and security coverage warrants selective pruning, not a numerical deletion target.

### 1. Required acceptance includes an optional paid-provider test — confirmed

**Evidence:** `scripts/acceptance.mjs:57` selects every browser spec except `core-journey.gated.spec.ts`. Its opening comment and `e2e/README.md` explicitly say it uses the real AI model.

The runner rejects skipped browser results and clears `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The result is a prerequisite conflict: ordinary required acceptance includes a deliberately optional provider evaluation.

**Why agents care:** An agent following the documented completion path can get blocked by an unrelated optional service, or investigate a provider failure while validating local code.

**Fix:** Explicitly separate deterministic required browser specs from opt-in provider evaluations. Keep strict skip rejection within the deterministic suite.

### 2. Merge enforcement is not established — confirmed locally; remote protection unknown

**Evidence:** No `.github` directory exists in this checkout. `package.json:13–14` exposes local acceptance commands. `scripts/acceptance.mjs:10–15` records revision and environment evidence; `scripts/acceptance.test.ts:8–22` tests stale-build rejection.

**Why agents care:** “Checks were run” remains procedural rather than an enforced property of the submitted revision.

**Fix:** Add one required hermetic PR check running privacy, unit tests, lint and build. Require it through repository rules and protect the current PR head. Run database acceptance against a disposable backend separately.

**Uncertainty:** I did not inspect GitHub branch rules or externally configured CI. Their absence cannot be inferred from this checkout.

### 3. Historical SQL text is used as a security oracle — confirmed

**Evidence:** `lib/finance/chat-publication-migration.test.ts:5–10` asserts five substrings in one historical migration. A later migration could restore unsafe permissions and this test would still pass.

History shows commit `0ac6c566` introduced this alongside a 75-line live publication test. That live test file is absent today. I did not establish whether its full behavioral coverage moved elsewhere.

**Why agents care:** This example teaches agents to prove security by searching source text. It produces green checks without demonstrating the promised protection.

**Fix:** Replace the text test with a current-schema regression: authenticated owners cannot publish assistant replies or invoke trusted publication; the trusted service can publish only valid evidence. Exercise it during migration replay.

**Related distinction:** Keep `lib/finance/currency-precision-contract.test.ts:5–11` for now. It compares the complete SQL currency map with application behavior, so it has more value than loose substring checks. Its reliance on a historical migration still deserves eventual replacement with current-schema parity.

### 4. Performance evidence exists without a latency guard — confirmed

**Evidence:** `supabase/tests/import-batch-throughput.mjs:39–52` measures fixture time, memory delta and payload sizes. Assertions cover row preservation, exact amounts and bounded candidate counts. Lines 64 and 73–74 check planner behavior and cleanup. There is no latency-budget assertion.

**Fix:** Add one deterministic import workload with a fixed synthetic fixture and a generous payload/work-count budget. Measure latency on a controlled disposable-backend runner; establish a baseline before choosing a threshold. Print the measured value, allowed value and workload on failure.

**Commands run:**

- `npx vitest run`
- `npx vitest run --reporter=verbose`

| Measurement | First run | Second run |
|---|---:|---:|
| Duration | 29.79 s | 28.21 s |
| Passing files | 288 | 288 |
| Skipped files | 8 | 8 |
| Passing tests | 1,591 | 1,591 |

**Why agents care:** Deleting small assertions will not necessarily improve startup or import cost. Disabling isolation could also introduce order dependence.

**Fix:** Profile expensive import chains before changing test architecture. Keep isolation by default. Do not claim a slowest-file ranking from this investigation: verbose output was truncated, so I did not obtain a reliable ranking.

**Evidence:** `AGENTS.md:22` requires a failing test for every bug fix. `AGENTS.md:82` prescribes final checks but gives no rule distinguishing behavioral protection from implementation mirroring.

`lib/all-pages.test.ts:31–43` tests a worthwhile concurrency bound using a real 1 ms timer and an exact peak of six, despite guidance against sleeps.

**Why agents care:** Agents can satisfy the instruction mechanically by asserting source strings, incidental call shapes or timing details.

**Fix:** Add the wording below. Replace that timer with explicitly controlled promises while preserving the concurrency protection.

**Root-cause limits:** History confirms the migration-text test was introduced as part of a real security fix, alongside stronger coverage. That supports a pattern of redundant “extra assurance,” not proof of a particular prompt causing sprawl. Recent commits such as `675b9a87` and `1bb943f8` also show browser expectation maintenance, but their subjects alone do not establish pointless tests.

- **Remove `lib/finance/chat-publication-migration.test.ts` after verifying or restoring executable permission coverage.** Its historical substrings cannot prove current security. The replacement current-schema test must cover the behavior first.
- **Remove `scalable-trading.gated.spec.ts` from deterministic required selection.** Retain the spec as an explicitly invoked provider evaluation.
- **Remove the timer block in `lib/all-pages.test.ts:36`.** Controlled promises can preserve the same concurrency guarantee without elapsed-time dependence.

I would not recommend deleting whole component, route or financial test groups from the evidence gathered.

- One current-schema trusted-publication permission regression, if equivalent coverage is absent.
- One fixed-workload performance budget with actionable failure output.
- Explicit deterministic versus paid-provider acceptance selection.

Replace the blanket regression-test sentence and extend validation with:

> **Tests protect behavior.** For a bug fix, first reproduce the failure at the smallest useful boundary. Add a regression test when it protects money, permissions, privacy, retained history, recovery, or a meaningful user workflow. State the concrete failure it catches.

- Disable Vitest isolation globally for a suggested three-second saving.
- Add blanket coverage targets, snapshots or a new testing framework.
- Split files solely because they are large.

- Run these database scripts against the owner’s installation.

- **Tests that grep migration files are weeds.** We both named `chat-publication-migration.test.ts` and both said to keep `currency-precision-contract.test.ts`.

- **AGENTS.md needs a rule for what a test is worth.** Our drafts say nearly the same thing: test money, permissions, privacy and history; don't assert copy, grep source or mirror the implementation; no sleeps; real providers opt-in only.
- **Don't add a new framework, coverage targets or snapshots, and don't delete half the tests because Theo did.**

1. **An orphan test guarding a removed feature, which is a better example than either of us first gave.** `chat-publication-migration.test.ts` was added in `0ac6c566` alongside a 75-line live test. Commit `1b06d686` later removed the whole feature and its live test, but left the grep test behind. It now asserts text in an old migration for a path the app no longer uses. Sol's fix was to write a new permission test to replace it; I'd just delete it, since the feature is gone. This is the cleanup rule AGENTS.md needs: "when you remove a feature, remove its tests."
2. **`lib/all-pages.test.ts:36` uses a real 1 ms timer** to test a concurrency limit. That's a small fix: use controlled promises.
3. **`supabase/tests/import-batch-throughput.mjs` already measures import time and memory** but never fails on them. It's a ready-made base for the DB performance check, so we don't need a new script.
4. **About 61% of unit-test time is module imports, not test code.** So deleting small tests won't make the suite much faster. Sol measured about 29 s on a warm run (my 69 s was a cold first run with the JSON reporter on).

- **Fail-closed QA identity.** I found that E2E can fall back to signing in as you, the owner. Sol didn't look, because I told it not to touch E2E. It's still a priority for me because it protects your real data.

1. CI, plus the merged AGENTS.md test rules (mostly Sol's wording, plus "remove a feature's tests with it" and "never delete or skip a failing test to get green").

I'd remove about 48 of the 60 browser tests, about 20 component tests, and the whole acceptance gate. Keep the tests that guard money, privacy and data loss.

## The plan
1. **Add CI.** Every PR runs privacy, lint, type-check, unit tests and build, with no database or AI key needed. A PR with failing tests can't merge.
2. **Add test rules to AGENTS.md.** A test must catch a real bug; no copy/label tests, no grepping source; delete a feature's tests with the feature; never delete or skip a failing test just to get green.
3. **Make browser tests safe.** They refuse to run unless signed in as the QA user, so they can't touch your data.
4. **Delete weak tests** (list below).
5. **Add one performance check.** Budgets on JS size per page and on network requests on Home, plus a time budget in the existing import throughput script.

## Delete

**Gate and grep tests**
- `scripts/acceptance.mjs`, `acceptance-results.mjs`, `acceptance.test.ts`, and the `acceptance:*` npm scripts. This gate blocks on optional tests; CI replaces it.
- `lib/finance/chat-publication-migration.test.ts`. It guards a feature that was removed on Oct 20.
- `app/plan/assumptions.test.ts`, the block that greps the SQL.

**Component tests that only check labels**
- `app/agent-briefing`, `first-steps`, `home-history`, `home-grid`, `home-cards`, `loading`
- `app/settings/phone-access-card`, `app/ai/artifacts/[id]/artifact-chat`
- `components/ai-panel`, `app-shell` (the render part), `chat-workspace`, `chat-messages`, `review-verification`, `voice-call`
- Large page tests (`app/page`, `plan/page`, `wealth`, `accounts`, `mission-control`, `ai-message`): delete the label checks and keep the money checks.

**Browser specs** (each one's behaviour is already tested in unit or SQL tests, or it is one feature inside a bigger journey)
- **Import:** `agent-team`, `import-history`, `import-undo`, `import-unicode`, `import-row-review`, `import-row-undo`, `import-organization`, `workbook-scope`
- **Goals and budgets:** `goal-plans`, `goal-reservations`, `budget-rollover`, `budget-completeness`, `forecast-preferences`, `scenario-history`, `source-coverage`
- **Balances and recurring payments:** `recurring-occurrences`, `recurring-source`, `coverage-recurring`, `dated-overview`, `pending-holds`, `reviewed-balances`, `verified-links`
- **Accounts and wealth:** `account-liquidity`, `wealth`, `scalable-history`, `money-editing`, `saved-view-scope`
- **Settings:** `settings-draft`, `settings-outage`, `auth-refresh`
- **Chat and reviews:** `review-freshness`, `investigation`, `provider-stop`, `evidence-room`, `chat-drafts`, `mne024`
- **Home and navigation:** `overview-navigation`, `home-cash-flow`, `home-drag` (folded into `home-dashboard`), `sync-on-open`
- **Old core journey:** `core-journey.gated` (the big mixed real/mocked journey)
- **Move to opt-in, out of normal runs:** `net-worth-chat`, `scalable-trading` (both use real AI)

## Keep (about 12 browser specs)
- Import: `import-journey`, `import-control`, `action-preview` (card applies once)
- Money and privacy: `net-worth`, `two-user-isolation`, `artifact-page-protection`
- Look and resilience: `theme-contrast`, `accessibility` (mobile), `bad-links`
- Features: `home-dashboard`, `artifact-home`, `chat-background`/`chat-cancel`
- Smoke: `core-journey.smoke`, without its health check

Also keep all `lib/finance`, import, SQL/RLS, migration replay, concurrency and `.live` DB tests, and the chat permission tests.

## Fix rather than delete
- `lib/all-pages.test.ts`: uses a real timer.
- `voice-call-controller.test.ts`: takes 24 s.
- `conflict-errcode.test.ts` stays: it's a cheap guard against the 18-hour retry outage (#131).

## How deletions are made safe
In the PR, I'll check each deleted browser spec against the SQL and unit tests that cover it. If something important isn't covered anywhere, I'll add one small unit or SQL test instead. I'll also sweep the remaining ~250 `lib/` unit tests with the same rule and list every removal in the PR description, so you can restore any one.

This is four PRs: CI + AGENTS.md, safe E2E, deletions, then perf. Should I start?
Sure go ahead

- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts with a test that fails on the current code. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's workspace. Browser tests use the QA user (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`) or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop the database: that is the owner's financial history.
